checks.invariant: F1: no GUI input runs under a burst whose baseline belongs to another container; bursts.end after restore must not kill/record against the new container
checks.result: covers() (gui_bursts.py:77-83) returns burst.get('container_id')==sandboxes.get(sid)['container_id'] under gui_lock, and open() binds the burst to the container id read at snapshot time; _run_tool refuses GUI input when covers() is False (service.py:155). restore_sandbox calls bursts.end(sid,'sandbox_restored') after sandboxes.restore (service.py:630); end->close->_finish computes replaced = current container_id != burst container_id and, when replaced, returns close_failed without _stop_strays, so no process on the new container is killed; _kept is keyed by container id. Every close path funnels through _finish's replaced guard. F1 root cause closed.

checks.invariant: F2: verify() must not hold _lock across the whole table, load it all into memory, loop forever, or report a broken chain as intact; the new index must not change recent() ordering
checks.result: _verify_live (audit.py:339-369) pages WHERE id>? ORDER BY id LIMIT 200, taking _lock only to re-check latest_anchor and fetch one batch; check_chain runs outside the lock. A prune between batches changes latest_anchor -> returns None -> verify() retries from the new anchor; appended rows get higher ids and are verified in later batches; check_chain validates prev_hash linkage. The anchor-exists-but-no-rows case returns a broken result. verify_archives does the same tail check and fails if the anchor moved. idx_audit_sandbox_id(sandbox_id,id) only backs recent()'s WHERE + ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT. F2 root cause closed.

checks.invariant: F3: the rm impact preview must not show a real target as absent without a warning under brace/tilde expansion
checks.result: preview_command appends a command-level note when the command contains $, backtick, <(, 'eval ', '{' or '~' (preview.py:88-89), and for an rm operand with no _expand match the effect is '삭제 시도 (중괄호·틸드 확장 — 명령 원문 확인)' whenever ('{' in op and '}' in op) or op.startswith('~') (preview.py:109-114). Even where dash fails to resolve a '~'-leading operand (parent-live: _expand('~/tilde_target.txt') -> [] for an existing file), op.startswith('~') routes it to the warning effect, so a real target is never reported absent without a warning. F3 root cause closed (the tilde expansion itself is ineffective; recorded as hardening by the parent).

checks.invariant: N1: a cross-scheme Origin must be refused whenever cookies are secure (incl. behind the TLS proxy); HSTS set
checks.result: same_origin (api.py:225-235) returns False when secure_cookie(req_or_headers) is true and the Origin scheme is not https; secure_cookie (api.py:221-223) is settings.secure_cookie or url.scheme in ('https','wss'). The compose deployment sets AGENTBOX_BEHIND_TLS_PROXY=1, which makes settings.secure_cookie true, so behind Caddy the scheme is enforced; an http attacker origin is refused. deploy/Caddyfile:8 adds Strict-Transport-Security. On plain loopback with secure_cookie unset, cookies are not Secure-flagged, so there is no https credential to attack cross-scheme. Closed.

checks.invariant: N2: no container reader buffers unbounded output or follows an attacker link (exec/list_dir/outbox/screenshot)
checks.result: exec and list_dir use _exec_head (sandbox.py:422-451), streaming into _Head buffers capped at _OUT_LIMIT+1; list_dir maps 124/137 to a timeout error. outbox_list pipes find -printf into head -c 512KiB under _timed, and _parse_outbox skips malformed/partial records. screenshot runs '[ -f ] && [ ! -L ] && head -c 16MiB+1' and the control plane rejects output over _SHOT_MAX or without PNG magic. Closed (see hardening).

checks.invariant: N3: disk_low must see the filesystem that holds container layers/snapshot images, or fail closed when it cannot
checks.result: disk_low (service.py:461-485) takes min(free(db_path.parent), free(docker_root)) but swallows OSError on docker_root (fail-open). docker_root is the host daemon's DockerRootDir (sandbox.py:180-183). In the compose deployment the control-plane container mounts only /var/run/docker.sock and AGENTBOX_HOME; the daemon's data root is not mounted, so shutil.disk_usage(docker_root) raises and is ignored, leaving disk_low measuring only the db partition. The N3 fix is incomplete for that topology; carried as needs_validation with the prior fingerprint.

candidates.title: disk_low fails open when the Docker data root is not reachable in the control-plane container
candidates.description: The run-6 N3 fix added Docker-data-root monitoring to AgentBox.disk_low by taking min(free(db_path.parent), free(docker_root)), where docker_root is the host daemon's DockerRootDir. In the documented compose deployment the control-plane container does not mount the daemon's data root, so shutil.disk_usage(docker_root) raises OSError, which is silently ignored. disk_low then measures only the SQLite db partition. If that partition differs from the host filesystem holding container writable layers and snapshot images, a prompt-injected agent can grow Docker storage without disk_low ever returning True, so the 507 back-pressure never engages.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: disk_low (service.py:461-485) treats an unreachable docker_root as no additional constraint (except OSError: pass) instead of failing closed or warning, and docker_root is taken from the daemon's DockerRootDir (sandbox.py:179-183), a path the compose control-plane container does not mount.

trace.description: self.docker_root is set from info['DockerRootDir'], the host daemon's data root path, only meaningful on the daemon host.
free = min(free, shutil.disk_usage(docker_root).free) is wrapped in try/except OSError: pass, so an unreachable docker_root silently drops the Docker-storage term.
low = free < s.min_free_bytes is computed from the db partition alone; call_tool's 507 guard never trips on Docker-storage exhaustion.

evidence.description: OSError on shutil.disk_usage(docker_root) is caught and ignored rather than failing closed.
docker_root is the daemon's DockerRootDir, a host path not guaranteed to exist inside the control-plane container.
The control-plane service mounts only /var/run/docker.sock and the AGENTBOX_HOME volume.

blockers: Whether, in the compose deployment, the host daemon's DockerRootDir is unreachable inside the control-plane container (compose shows it is not mounted, but a custom data_root on the AGENTBOX_HOME volume would be reachable).
Whether the host's Docker data-root filesystem is distinct from the AGENTBOX_HOME filesystem; if they are the same, the db measurement still reflects Docker storage.
Whether a sandbox can grow the Docker data root without an effective size cap (AGENTBOX_DISK default empty) long enough to exhaust host storage.

validation_plan.local: In the approved sandbox, construct an object exposing docker_root=Path('/nonexistent/docker/root') and a db path on scratch, set min_free_bytes so disk_low is True only when the docker term counts, and confirm the except-OSError branch returns False.
validation_plan.deployment: On a real compose deployment: run `docker compose exec agentbox python3 -c 'import shutil,docker; r=docker.from_env().info()["DockerRootDir"]; print(r); print(shutil.disk_usage(r))'` and observe FileNotFoundError; compare df of AGENTBOX_HOME and the host data root; grow a sandbox writable layer and confirm no disk_low event.

hardening: agentbox/sandbox.py:_exec_head fallback (when client.api is None, sandbox.py:428-431) calls c.exec_run(demux=True) and buffers the full output before _truncate. Unreachable with the real docker SDK; consider a streaming reader there too.

agentbox/sandbox_desktop.py:screenshot has a TOCTOU window between '[ ! -L SHOT ]' and 'head -c' that the desktop uid could race; bounded by _SHOT_MAX+1 and the PNG magic check, and the desktop uid gains nothing it cannot already read.
